# `Q-2-49` — Bracketed text renders without its brackets

> `[...]` is span syntax in quarto-markdown. A bracket group with no
> attribute block after it renders as an empty span, and the brackets
> themselves are discarded.

## What this means

In quarto-markdown, square brackets introduce a span:

```markdown
[important]{.highlight}
```

The `[...]` half supplies the content and the `{...}` half supplies the
attributes. When the attribute block is missing, the span is still
parsed — but it has nothing to say, so it renders as

```html
<span>important</span>
```

and the brackets you wrote are gone.

That is usually harmless formatting noise. Occasionally it changes what
the document *says*:

```markdown
The default subject prefix is "[Posit Connect]".
```

renders as

> The default subject prefix is "Posit Connect".

which documents the wrong value. Quarto 1 rendered these brackets
literally, so this most often appears in documents ported from Quarto 1.

Other shapes that hit the same rule:

```markdown
Requires Posit Connect [Version TBD] or later.
Upon an initial user session [1], the server creates a cookie [2].
```

## How to fix

If you meant the brackets literally, escape them:

```markdown
The default subject prefix is "\[Posit Connect\]".
```

Both Quarto 1 and Quarto 2 render `\[...\]` as literal brackets, and
Quarto 2 produces no span node at all for the escaped form — so
re-running the fix is safe.

If you meant a span, add the attribute block:

```markdown
[important]{.highlight}
```

`qmd-syntax-helper` can find and fix these in bulk. Because escaping is
a source edit that cannot afterwards be told apart from your own intent,
run `check` first and read what it proposes:

```bash
qmd-syntax-helper check   -r literal-brackets "docs/**/*.qmd"
qmd-syntax-helper convert -r literal-brackets --in-place "docs/**/*.qmd"
```

## If your project uses bare spans on purpose

A bare span is a usable marker for a Lua filter to rewrite. If that is
what your project does, say so once in `_quarto.yml` rather than
escaping every occurrence:

```yaml
diagnostics:
  Q-2-49:
    level: off
    reason: "bare spans are markers for our annotate.lua filter"
```

See [suppressing diagnostics](../../guides/publishing/index.qmd#suppressing-diagnostics).
